Get started

Install Sigma Loop for your host, then run /sigma-init once in each repository you want it to work on.

On this page
  • Pick your host
  • Claude Code
  • Codex
  • Cursor
  • Antigravity
  • What /sigma-init does

You need git, bash and python3 (standard library only). The GitHub CLI gh, logged in, is optional: it is needed for GitHub issues as the backlog, a Projects board, or a pull request per goal. A local-files backlog needs none of it.

Pick your host

Claude Code Codex Cursor Antigravity

Claude Code

  1. Install

    claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/Agrim-Intelligence/sigma
claude plugin install sigmaloop@sigmaloop

  2. Initialise

    Restart the session, then run this from the root of the repository you want Sigma to work on.

    /sigma-init --demo
/sigma-loop

--demo queues a runnable demo goal; /sigma-loop then runs it through all the phases. To run in Claude Code's cloud, read Cloud sessions first.

Codex

  1. Install

    codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/Agrim-Intelligence/sigma
codex plugin add sigmaloop@sigmaloop

  2. Initialise

    Run this from the root of your repository. The flag makes AGENTS.md carry the standing rules.

    /sigma-init --codex --demo

Measured: the install and the first loop command, in a real Codex session. Not measured: a complete goal through to a merged pull request. Details on Hosts.

If the slash command is not available

Run the init flow directly from the root of your repository. This is a path you type; <installed-sigma> is the installed plugin directory.

python3 <installed-sigma>/skills/sigma-init/scripts/init_flow.py . --codex --demo

Cursor

  1. Install

    git clone https://github.com/Agrim-Intelligence/sigma ~/sigma

  2. Initialise

    Cursor has no plugin install: clone to a folder outside the project you are adopting. Then, from the root of your own repository:

    /sigma-init --cursor --demo

Measured in the Cursor app: set-up with a Projects board, and one real issue to a merged pull request (merged by hand). Not measured: the loop on several goals. Details on Hosts.

If the slash command is not available

Run the init flow directly from the root of your repository. This is a path you type; <installed-sigma> is the folder you cloned to.

python3 ~/sigma/skills/sigma-init/scripts/init_flow.py . --cursor --demo

Antigravity

  1. Install

    agy plugin install https://github.com/Agrim-Intelligence/sigma

  2. Initialise

    Then, inside agy, from the root of your own repository:

    /sigma-init --antigravity

Measured in agy: the install and set-up with a Projects board and an AGENTS.md. Not measured: a goal run or the loop. Details on Hosts.

If the slash command is not available

Run the init flow directly from the root of your repository. This is a path you type; <installed-sigma> is the installed plugin directory.

python3 <installed-sigma>/skills/sigma-init/scripts/init_flow.py . --antigravity

What /sigma-init does

Run it once in every repository, on every host. It is safe to re-run: it does not ask an answered question again.

  • Checks git and gh access.
  • Asks where your backlog lives (local goal files or GitHub issues) and which command runs your tests.
  • Scaffolds the .sdlc folder and ends by printing the next command to run.

On Codex, Cursor and Antigravity there is no interactive question: the flow prints each open one as an [ask] line with the flag that answers it.
